sample.pageIntro: Sample sets to verify the format and quality of data captured with the RootLens iOS app. New versions will be added as recording conditions and contributor scale expand.
sample.heroSubtitle: 48 first-person video clips of household tasks with per-frame 3D hand pose, wrist 6-DoF actions, and natural-language action labels.
sample.s1p1Lead: 48 clips of household tasks recorded with the RootLens iOS app from a head-mounted camera in Japan. All faces are blurred. Each frame contains:
s1p1Items: 21 hand joints in 3D per hand, in MANO canonical hand-local coordinates (`observation.hand_keypoints_3d`)
`task_index` into `meta/tasks.jsonl` pointing to a natural-language action label
sample.s2p1: LeRobotDataset v3.0 format. Standard loaders read this layout without modification.
sample.s3p1: Each frame's `task_index` maps to an action label in `meta/tasks.jsonl`. Labels are present-tense English sentences describing hand movements and objects (e.g. "Right hand reaches for the kettle handle."). Each clip is segmented into multiple labels at action transitions.
sample.s3p2: Labels are generated from video frames by a vision-language model.
sample.episodesSubheading: All 48 episodes. Click to play; expand a panel to read every action label with its timestamp.
sample.s4p1Lead: The next sample will add captures from roughly a dozen Japan-based TestFlight beta contributors:
s4p1Items: `observation.state` : camera 6-DoF in the ARKit world frame
`depth/{frame_index:06d}.png` : LiDAR depth maps on supported devices

hero.description: RootLens is a physical-AI project born at the University of Osaka. We monetize work data from Japan's commercial workplaces and return the benefits, in many forms, to the workplaces themselves.

problem.title: Robots learn by watching people. The footage is missing.
problem.p1: Teaching a robot to work takes video of people actually working. Just as text-generating AI learned from a vast amount of text, robots learn from video of human motion.
problem.p2: But usable work footage is in critically short supply. Video collected in prepared settings tends to look nothing like a real workplace, and it costs time and money.
problem.p3: The data that works is produced in the course of everyday operations, on site.

step1.label: Work as usual
step1.text: Staff wearing a headgear camera work normal part-time shifts. Dishwashing, prep, plating: any job where the headgear isn't in the way.

step2.label: Footage becomes training data
step2.text: Video recorded during shifts becomes material robots learn manipulation from. The store's operations don't change at all.

step3.label: Stores get paid
step3.text: We pay the store a filming fee for the hours actually recorded, so it keeps the extra hands while holding labor costs down.

footer.builtBy: Built by Yudai Mori and Akito Kawano

math.note: Example at a ¥1,200 hourly wage. The fee is paid per recorded hour. ¥500 is the current base rate; we raise it as data sales grow, aiming for zero effective cost.

enterprise.label: SERVICE 02 · FOR COMPANIES
enterprise.title: Start with a workplace diagnostic
enterprise.p1: For companies considering robots or physical AI. We bring the capture equipment and app, record the work on your floor, and deliver a diagnostic report, free of charge: which steps suit automation and what adoption would take.
enterprise.p2: It can be free because only the data you approve is sold as training data, and that revenue covers the diagnostic. All we ask of the site is the recording.

model.label: HOW IT WORKS
model.title: Collect, sell, give back
model.p1: Work data has buyers. Robotics companies are searching worldwide for training footage. But it is not realistic for a shop or a factory to sell its own data: that takes capture equipment, rights handling, and sales channels.
model.p2: RootLens takes that part on. We sell the work data collected on site to robotics companies and return a share of the revenue to the workplace, through two services shaped to each site.
model.emphasis: All we ask of the workplace: keep working as usual.

devices.label: FOR DATA BUYERS
devices.title: Capture rigs and data specs
devices.intro1: Robot training can't use just any video. It needs footage focused on the work itself, shot in real environments, from as many different sites as possible. RootLens data is collected in shops and workplaces that are actually in business.
devices.intro2: We grow the lineup rig by rig. One set is in operation today.

set01.name: iPhone Pro + headgear
set01.desc: An iPhone Pro mounted on the worker's head records first-person video while ARKit runs alongside. We use iPhone 15 Pro or later Pro models; specs below are measured on an iPhone 15 Pro.
set01.s2v: LiDAR depth maps, 256×192 at 15 fps, synced with RGB; 16-bit integers, depth values in mm; ARKit confidence maps (3 levels) included
set01.s3v: Continuous 6DoF camera poses from ARKit visual-inertial odometry (VIO), in a consistent world frame; tracking state and trajectory included
set01.s5v: All modalities registered to a common high-resolution timestamp
set01.s6v: Camera intrinsics for RGB and depth; coordinate-frame TF included
set01.s7v: ARKit mesh anchors and point cloud
set01.s8v: Continuous clips from a few minutes up to about 30 min (to date); roughly 0.2 to 0.3 GB per minute as MCAP
set01.s9v: Face blurring with EgoBlur; no audio recorded
set01.s10v: Written site agreements; per-clip consent records

set02.name: Smart glasses
set02.desc: A lightweight glasses-based rig is in preparation, with more sets to follow.
